{{Quote|What's up there?''"<br />[Treadwell burps a noncommittal reply]<br />"''I know ''you'' don't know, you maniac. Where're my macrobinoculars?|Luke Skywalker and Treadwell, spotting a space battle above Tatooine|<ref name="Wind" />}}
'''WED-15-77''', or simply '''Treadwell''', was a [[WED-15 Treadwell droid/Legends|WED-15 Treadwell]] [[Maintenance droid/Legends|repair droid]] that was built prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], serving [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]] [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] for more than twenty [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. Treadwell often worked with Lars's nephew, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], on the [[Moisture vaporator/Legends|moisture vaporators]] of the [[Lars homestead/Legends|family's farm]]. While working on a vaporator with Skywalker one day in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] suffered a meltdown, and Skywalker, eager to meet his friend [[Laze Loneozner/Legends|Fixer]] at [[Tosche Station/Legends|Tosche Station]] near the [[City/Legends|settlement]] of [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]], abandoned the droid in the [[Desert/Legends|desert]]. Treadwell was subsequently taken by the [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]] of the desert.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Come on, Treadwell, get yourself over to the landspeeder. I've gotta get into Anchorhead and tell Fixer about this!|Luke Skywalker, to Treadwell|<ref name="Wind" />}}
[[File:Treadwell-Luke-TJ.jpg|thumb|left|250px|WED-15-77 helping Luke Skywalker]]
WED-15-77, also known as Treadwell, was a [[WED-15 Treadwell droid/Legends|WED-15 Treadwell]] [[Maintenance droid/Legends|repair droid]] that was produced by<ref name="DB" /> [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]], one of the two largest [[Droid/Legends|droid]] manufacturing companies in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="TEGTTD" /> Prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], which [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|broke out]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the droid began to serve [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]] [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars's]] [[Lars family/Legends|family]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Treadwell worked with the [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] at the [[Lars homestead/Legends|Lars homestead]] until the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who had built C-3PO as a child, visited the Lars family and took the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] away.<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref>

Treadwell continued to serve the Lars family for more than twenty [[Standard year/Legends|years]], into the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Treadwell liked to work with [[Beru Whitesun Lars/Legends|Beru Lars]], Owen's [[Marriage/Legends|wife]], who gave the droid the same simple and predictable jobs. The droid often helped Lars's nephew, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], in a variety of chores,<ref name="DB" /> such as repairing [[Moisture vaporator/Legends|moisture vaporators]] out in the [[Desert/Legends|desert]]. Early in the civil war&mdash;not much before [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]], a Tatooinian farmboy, was about to leave for the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]]&mdash;Treadwell broke down. Skywalker took parts of the droid to [[Laze Loneozner/Legends|Laze "Fixer" Loneozner]],<ref name="crucible">[[Star Wars (1977) 17|''Star Wars'' (1977) 17]]</ref> one of his childhood friends, who worked as a mechanic near the [[City/Legends|settlement]] of [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]].<ref name="Wind">{{SWRadio|A Wind to Shake the Stars}}</ref> However, Fixer had a week's backlog, and he couldn't begin working on the droid.<ref name="crucible" /> Finally, the Treadwell got repaired and returned to work. One day in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Lars asked Skywalker to service the vaporator units on the [[Farm/Legends|farm's]] south ridge with the help of Treadwell.<ref name="Wind" />

During the work, Treadwell used an uninsulated [[Limb/Legends|manipulator]] and consequently received an electric shock. Not much later, Skywalker spotted a [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|space battle]] above the planet. He ran to his [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] and called for the droid to follow him,<ref name="Wind" /> but Treadwell's [[Engine/Legends|engine]] exploded,<ref name="life">''[[A New Hope: The Life of Luke Skywalker]]''</ref> and the droid suffered a final meltdown.<ref name="DB" /> For a moment Skywalker hesitated about leaving the droid behind, but since the vital components of Treadwell were shot, he left the smoking droid in the desert<ref name="EP4NOVEL" /> and decided to pick him up on the way home. He raced off to [[Tosche Station/Legends|Tosche Station]] near Anchorhead to tell Fixer about the battle.<ref name="Wind" /> Treadwell, meanwhile, was taken by the [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]] of the desert and, as a result, was not there when Skywalker went to retrieve it.<ref name="EP4NOVEL" />

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Treadwell, clamp these two leads together while I splice them.''"<br />[Treadwell maneuvering, still gobbling to itself]<br />"''No, no, you idiot! Use your ''insulated'' arm!''"<br />[An electronic shriek of surprise and distress. Circuitry sputters]<br />"''Release! Release! Back off!|Luke Skywalker and Treadwell|<ref name="Wind" />}}
WED-15-77 was a typical [[Class five droid/Legends|class-five]] [[WED Treadwell repair droid/Legends|Treadwell repair droid]] with two rows of five treaded [[wheel]]s on its base. The droid had a very small independent thought processor<ref name="tcswe" /> but had enhanced binocular fine-focus vision, which helped it to spot circuitry damage. The droid's enhanced [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] were mounted on a long, telescopic stalk,<ref name="CVD" /> which also held six arms,<ref name="EP4NOVEL" /> including an equipment test arm and various manipulators,<ref name="CVD" /> at least one of which was insulated.<ref name="Wind" /> By 0 BBY, Treadwell's movements had become unsteady, and only three of its arms were functioning.<ref name="EP4NOVEL" />

Treadwell was capable of accomplishing even very specific tasks with close supervision, but it could not conduct complicated work on its own due to its limited intelligence.<ref name="CVD" /> It was a recalcitrant yet hardworking droid that preferred helping Beru Lars, since she gave the droid simple and predictable jobs.<ref name="DB" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Treadwell-bts.jpg|thumb|right|150px|John Barry's production sketch of WED-15-77]]
WED-15-77 was designed in [[1975]] by production designer [[John Barry]] for use in the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="making">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> The same droid model was also used for the droid [[WED-15-I662]] and for another, [[Unidentified WED-15 Treadwell (Lars homestead)|unnamed Treadwell]] during the filming of the movie.<ref name="DB" /> Barry's notes showed that the prop had one functioning arm and housed a radio controller in its treadwell base to allow for off-screen crew members to control it. Barry's sketch indicated that the model stood between four feet and four feet, six inches tall. Scenes featuring the droid were shot on location in [[Tunisia]] in [[March]] [[1976]].<ref name="making" />

While ''A New Hope'' was in post-production, Treadwell became the first of the film's droid characters to receive a voice from sound designer [[Ben Burtt]]. To create the vocalizations, Burtt combined electronic noises with sounds of himself speaking fake baby talk. Although crew members likened the noises to those of a talking chicken, [[George Lucas]] approved the sound effects. The droid's voice served as a template for following droid characters, including [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]].<ref name="GPB">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]</ref> The droid made its first appearance in the [[December]] 1976 [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']],<ref name="EP4NOVEL" /> ghostwritten by [[Alan Dean Foster]].<ref name="ANH novel SE">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]], [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|''Special Edition'']] foreword by [[George Lucas]]</ref> The droid was featured in a scene that was ultimately cut from the released version of ''A New Hope'', but it appeared in various adaptations of the film, including the movie's novelization<ref name="EP4NOVEL" /> and [[Star Wars (radio)|radio drama]].<ref name="Wind" /> Treadwell also appeared in the [[2002]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], becoming one of the few characters to appear in both the [[Original trilogy|original]]<ref name="btm">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> and the [[prequel trilogy]] of ''[[Star Wars]]'',<ref name="AOTC" /> although its scene had been cut from ''A New Hope''.<ref name="btm" />

WED-15-77's meltdown scene occurred before the appearance of a similar-looking unidentified Treadwell in the film.<ref name="DB" /> In the ''Star Wars'' radio drama, however, WED-15-77 merely stopped moving rather than melting down, and Owen Lars mentioned at a later [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] auction that he had "already got a Treadwell [and didn't] need [[WED-15-ST68/Legends|another]]." This suggested that the unidentified droid was intended to be WED-15-77<ref name="Giants">{{SWRadio|While Giants Mark Time}}</ref> and not another droid of the same line. However, the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] confirmed WED-15-77's meltdown to be final and the droids to be separate characters.<ref name="DB" />
